title: A filter array that isn't a valid AST reaches the driver as an opaque `where` — reject it at the protocol instead
body:
Item 2 of #3948, split out so that issue can close on its headline defect. **This is an error-locality improvement, not a correctness bug** — since #3948 item 1 the drivers throw, so nothing is silently dropped either way. What is wrong is *where* the error comes from and how much it tells you.

## Current behaviour

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:2849-2852`:

```ts
if (isFilterAST(parsedFilter)) {
  parsedFilter = parseFilterAST(parsedFilter);
}
options.where = parsedFilter;   // assigned unconverted when isFilterAST() said no
```

`isFilterAST` is consulted as a *conversion* gate, not a *validation* gate. An array that fails it is passed straight through as if it were an opaque `where` object. The driver then rejects it — with a driver-level message, several layers from the request that carried the malformed filter, and differently per backend.

A caller gets `[sql-driver] Unrecognized filter operator "…"` for what is really "your `$filter` query parameter is not a valid filter AST".

## Why this is worth doing

If a value *looks* like a filter array (`Array.isArray`) but `isFilterAST()` refuses it, that is a **malformed filter**, not an opaque `where`. Rejecting at the boundary gives:

- one error for every backend instead of three variants (driver-sql throws one message, driver-memory another, driver-mongodb passes `$${op}` to Mongo and surfaces a server error);
- a message that can name the offending operator *and* point at `VALID_AST_OPERATORS`, which the driver cannot do as usefully because it has already lost the request context;
- failure before any connection is taken.

## The trap to avoid

`isFilterAST` **does** accept nested arrays — `filter.zod.ts:516`:

```ts
// Legacy flat array: [[cond], [cond], ...]
if (filter.every((item: unknown) => isFilterAST(item))) return filter.length > 0;
```

So the naive form of this change does **not** break legitimate `[[field, op, value], [field, op, value]]` filters; they already return `true` and get parsed.

What it *would* newly reject is an array-shaped `where` that is not an AST at all — including any driver-specific extension a caller passes opaquely, if one exists. That makes this a **request-path narrowing**, which is why #3948 phrased it as *"Consider"* rather than a fix. It needs someone to decide whether an opaque array `where` is a supported input, and to say so in the error either way.

## Suggested shape

Reject only the unambiguous case — `Array.isArray(parsedFilter) && !isFilterAST(parsedFilter)` — with a 400-class error naming the first unrecognized operator it can find and referring to `VALID_AST_OPERATORS`. Object `where` values keep passing through untouched, so the `$`-token path is unaffected.

Worth a test that a nested `[[a,'=',1],[b,'=',2]]` filter still parses, since that is the regression this change could plausibly cause.

Split from #3948 (items 1 and 3 of which are done). Refs objectstack-ai/objectui#2945
